outlooks.summary: Severe storms are expected this afternoon through this evening across western portions of the central and southern Plains, capable of producing very large hail, a tornado threat, and damaging winds. Isolated severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts and some hail are possible this afternoon and evening from the Mid Atlantic region to southwest New England.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A broad synoptic trough will persist over the Great Lakes region and extend through the Ohio Valley to the southern Appalachians, while an upstream anticyclone across the southwest states remains centered over the lower Colorado Valley. Northwesterly flow aloft will extend from the northern Rockies through much of the Great Plains to the basal portion of the eastern U.S. trough.

sections.title: Central and southern High Plains
sections.text: Surface dewpoints in the upper 50s to middle 60s F reside across the central Plains and will be a source for moisture for the severe-weather threat expected across the western portions of the central and southern High Plains this afternoon through this evening, and may persist into tonight. Some cloudiness will be possible across a portion of the central Plains (from western SD to western NE) at the start of this forecast period. Meanwhile, diabatic heating west of these clouds combined with the aforementioned moisture and a plume of steep midlevel lapse rates (7.5-8.5 C/km) will result in a corridor of moderate to potentially strong instability (MLCAPE 2000-2500 J/kg) during the afternoon. Weak vorticity maxima embedded within the northwesterly flow regime, diabatic heating over the mountains and destabilization of the boundary layer should contribute to thunderstorm initiation over the higher terrain as well as along surface boundaries. In addition to a lee trough, a surface boundary extending from northwest KS to southeast WY will be a focus for storms this afternoon, with the available CAPE/strong shear parameter space supporting supercells with the initial development and all

sections.title: Middle Atlantic region to the Northeast States
sections.text: A cold front will advance east into the Northeast States and Middle Atlantic region today, with this boundary and a pre-frontal trough extending from central/eastern VA to the Hudson Valley region being the primary foci for thunderstorm development by this afternoon. Although midlevel lapse rates will remain weak, which will also temper the strength of updrafts, a corridor of moderate instability (MLCAPE 1500-2000 J/kg) is likely from the Middle Atlantic states through at least southwest New England. Forcing for ascent attendant to weak midlevel impulses embedded within southwesterly flow aloft and in vicinity of the surface boundaries should prove favorable for thunderstorm development by this afternoon. Winds through the lowest 3 km will remain modest, but a belt of 40-50 kt winds above 500-600 mb will support 35-45 kt effective bulk shear and the potential for storms to organize. Locally strong to damaging wind gusts and some hail appear likely with the severe storms from afternoon into early evening. ..Peters/Cook.. 07/27/2018

outlooks.summary: The greatest risk for severe storms today it evening will be over parts of the central High Plains. Strong to severe storms also should occur today over parts of the Mid-Atlantic and New England.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The mid/upper-level pattern this period will be dominated by two slow-moving features: a strong anticyclone over the lower Colorado River Valley, and a cyclone drifting eastward across that part of northern ON northeast of Lake Superior. Cyclonic flow associated with the ON low will cover much of the U.S. north of about I-40 and east of the High Plains. At the surface, 11Z chart analysis showed a cold front from northwestern OH southwestward across southern IN to central AR, becoming quasistationary from there over north-central TX and southern NM. The front should advance eastward across the Lower Great Lakes and western portions of NY/PA through the period, preceded by a prefrontal trough moving slowly eastward in the eastern Appalachians and their lee side. A weak low-level baroclinic zone will persist from the central High Plains southeastward across northern/eastern OK.

sections.title: Central High Plains
sections.text: Thunderstorms are expected to form over the Laramie and Front Ranges and adjacent higher terrain to the east this afternoon, initially with the potential for supercells offering hail, damaging gusts and a risk of a few tornadoes. Some of the hail may be significant/damaging in nature, especially from any supercells. Forecast soundings show strong deep-layer lapse rates juxtaposed with adequate low-level moisture and favorable wind profiles -- preconvective MLCAPE 2000-2500 J/kg, substantial directional shear beneath strong mid/upper flow, and 50-60 kt effective-shear magnitudes. Details vary among assorted operational/synoptic and convection-allowing progs on timing and location of greatest upscale growth this evening. Regardless, due to the favorable environment with strong storm-relative low-level flow and adequate low-level moisture, a strong consensus exists for aggregation of afternoon/evening convection into an MCS over the western NE/northeastern CO/northwestern KS region. Substantial southeastward to south-southeastward, forward-propagational component should occur across western KS, moving along and west of a low-level theta-e gradient. sections.title: Portions of Mid-Atlantic/New England
sections.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms should develop around midday to early afternoon over the higher terrain from northern WV to eastern NY and northern New England. This will occur as diabatic heating of higher terrain preferentially weakens MLCINH, amidst subtle low-level convergence near the prefrontal trough. Activity should increase in coverage through the remainder of the afternoon, filling into a northeast/southwest-oriented belt of scattered to numerous thunderstorms. The main threats will be damaging wind, some of which may become severe, along with sporadic hail. Small-scale shots of DCVA are possible from subtle vorticity lobes orbiting the main cyclone, and much of the outlook area will be under the right-entrance region of an 85-95-kt, cyclonically curved 250-mb jet. Associated destabilized lapse rates aloft will not be as steep as in an EML, with forecast soundings showing generally 6-7 deg C/km above the boundary layer. outlooks.summary: Numerous severe storms are expected this afternoon and evening across the central High Plains with very large hail, intense wind gusts, and a few tornadoes possible. Strong to isolated severe storms are anticipated across parts of the Northeast into early evening, with risks for hail and damaging winds.

sections.title: Central High Plains
sections.text: Scattered storms are expected to form over the Laramie and Front Ranges during the mid to late afternoon, with ongoing convection near the NE/CO border area also likely to increase and redevelop upshear through the afternoon. While boundary-layer moisture will not be particularly rich with surface dew points in the mid 50s to lower 60s, the eastern periphery of the elevated mixed layer will support moderate buoyancy with MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg. Low-level veering with height beneath strong mid/upper-level speed shear will favor rather large effective shear magnitudes around 50-55 kt. This should yield a few supercells, a couple of which may be intense and long-track to the southeast, mainly between 3-7 pm MDT. Very large hail and tornadoes will be most likely during this time frame. Storm-scale mergers/consolidation will likely yield an MCS developing near the CO/KS border area and moving south-southeast across western KS in the evening, eventually weakening in western OK to the eastern TX Panhandle vicinity later tonight. The risk for severe wind gusts will be greatest over western KS where bowing structures in the forward-propagating MCS are anticipated. The lack of even larger

sections.title: Northeast
sections.text: Scattered storms will develop this afternoon along and east of the central to northern Appalachians. This will occur as surface heating continues downstream of ongoing stratus most prominent across the Upper OH Valley through central PA, amid subtle low-level convergence near a pre-frontal trough. An extensive broken band of storms is expected by late afternoon to early evening. Mid to upper-level speed shear will favor high-level updraft rotation. This will compensate for poor lapse rates aloft and yield some risk for quarter to golf ball size hail. A warm/moist boundary layer will also foster a risk for strong wind gusts, especially as convection evolves into quasi-linear, multicell clusters amid small low-level hodographs. These hazards will diminish after sunset. ..Grams/Conliglio.. 07/27/2018

outlooks.summary: Numerous severe storms are expected this afternoon and evening across the central High Plains with very large hail, intense wind gusts, and a few tornadoes possible. Strong to isolated severe storms are anticipated across parts of the Northeast into early evening, with risks for hail and damaging winds.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Only minor changes have been made to the previous outlook and include the following: 1) Increased wind probabilities over portions of southeastern CO 2) Enveloped more of southeast CO into the OK Panhandle for a conditional severe risk of 65+ kt gusts 3) Included a small portion of central OK in the 5-percent wind probabilities given some recent model guidance showing an MCS moving into OK late tonight. 4) Included portions of central VA in 15-percent wind probabilities. Elsewhere, left the forecast unchanged. ..Smith.. 07/27/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT Fri Jul 27 2018/

sections.title: Northeast
sections.text: Scattered storms will develop this afternoon along and east of the central to northern Appalachians. This will occur as surface heating continues downstream of ongoing stratus most prominent across the Upper OH Valley through central PA, amid subtle low-level convergence near a pre-frontal trough. An extensive broken band of storms is expected by late afternoon to early evening. Mid to upper-level speed shear will favor high-level updraft rotation. This will compensate for poor lapse rates aloft and yield some risk for quarter to golf ball size hail. A warm/moist boundary layer will also foster a risk for strong wind gusts, especially as convection evolves into quasi-linear, multicell clusters amid small low-level hodographs. These hazards will diminish after sunset.

outlooks.summary: Severe storms producing damaging winds, some significantly strong, will spread across southeast Colorado through southwest Kansas to parts of the Oklahoma and northern Texas Panhandles to northwest Oklahoma this evening and tonight, while additional isolated severe storms occur farther northward through the central High Plains. Strong to isolated severe storms remain possible across a portion of the northern Mid Atlantic region to southern New England.

sections.title: Southern and central High Plains
sections.text: Short-term models, including the last several runs of the operational HRRR, continue to suggest upscale growth is likely of storms across eastern CO and western KS into a forward-propagating MCS through southwest KS this evening toward northwest OK later tonight. This scenario seems reasonable, given the strengthening of a southerly low-level jet into southwest KS, though latest deterministic guidance suggests the speed of the 850-mb jet will not be very strong. This combined with the lack of stronger downstream instability may tend to limit the overall coverage of stronger/ severe wind gusts. Nonetheless, objective analyses indicated DCAPE of 1000-1200 J/kg into southwest KS and the OK/TX Panhandles suggesting the potential for severe/damaging winds with any forward-propagating MCS. For these reasons, this outlook will maintain an Enhanced severe risk for severe winds, with an area of significant wind gusts possible from southeast CO through western KS to far northwest OK. sections.title: Southern New England to Delmarva
sections.text: Convection advancing east into residual marginal to moderate instability will continue to pose a threat for locally strong to damaging wind gusts, prior to the boundary layer stabilizing with the loss of daytime heating. ..Peters.. 07/28/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will develop in the next few hours and pose a threat for some wind damage and severe wind gusts, as well as marginally severe hail. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch is likely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong heating to the east of a cloud shield over the northern Appalachians and western Catskills has led to thunderstorm development along a weak trough/differential heating boundary. Sufficient deep-layer shear should support some storm organization in the form of small bowing segments and discrete cells with supercell characteristics, and steepening low-level lapse rates within upper 60s to low 70s dewpoints should support the threat for some damaging winds and severe wind gusts, with some severe hail potential in any rotation that can persist in the discrete storms. The coverage of the severe threat is likely large enough to need a Severe Thunderstorm Watch in the next hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms will increase in coverage the next few hours over the area. The main threats are severe wind gusts and marginally severe hail. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Heating from the eastern Appalachians to the Chesapeake Bay area amidst low-to-mid 60s dewpoints over WV to mid-to-upper 70s dewpoints over the east has contributed to moderate instability with little remaining convective inhibition. A subtle shortwave rounding the base of the upper low and lift in the frontal zone now crossing western WV has led to rather early thunderstorm development over that area, with additional thunderstorms now forming in the vicinity of a weak pre-frontal trough over central VA and in the very moist air mass over eastern VA. Given sufficient deep-layer shear magnitudes and mostly straight hodographs, storms are expected to have a mixed multicell/discrete supercell characteristics in the early part of the event, with a few more line/bowing segments developing as storms mature. Both severe wind gusts and marginally severe hail will be possible with the stronger storms through the afternoon, the coverage of which is expected to be large enough to need a Severe Thunderstorm Watch over at least portions of the area in the next hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms capable of wind damage and marginally severe hail will continue to move over the area this afternoon. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch may be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms have developed and persisted on the eastern edge of a cloud shield, with some forcing for ascent provided by the right entrance region of a mid-to-upper level jet crossing the area. Deep-layer shear has been sufficient to support some supercell/bowing characteristics over northern Somerset county the last half hour, which could pose the risk for marginally severe hail and damaging wind in the next hour. Additional organized modes are possible with the additional storms lining up to the southwest of the current supercell. However, rather weak instability/mid-level lapse rates are expected to temper the overall severe threat over this area compared to areas farther southwest in which Watches were issued. Therefore it is not clear if a Severe Thunderstorm Watch will be needed over this area, but trends in storm organization and destabilization over the cloud-free areas will be monitored closely for an increase in overall severe potential that may require a Severe Thunderstorm Watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to further intensify over western Nebraska and far northeast Colorado this afternoon, with an increasing threat of large hail, severe wind gusts, and a couple tornadoes. Watch issuance is expected within the next hour or so.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of loosely organized storms has persisted across far northeast Colorado and the Nebraska Panhandle through mid-day. Further low-level warm advection, augmented by weak east/southeast upslope trajectories, should maintain this cluster and support new development (especially along the upshear flank) early this afternoon. While storms have been slow to intensify due to a relatively modest thermodynamic environment, increasing insolation (yielding upwards of 2000-2500 J/kg of MLCAPE) southeast of this cluster should favor gradual organization/deepening of cores through mid afternoon. Although an 18Z LBF sounding sampled weak low-level flow, increasing northwesterly winds at mid/upper levels will combine with adequate directional shear to likely support supercell clusters and one or more bowing segments accelerating southeast. Such a mode evolution will favor severe winds as the main threat, with an increasing potential of intense gusts (75+ mph) as cells move into Kansas. Very large hail will also be possible with semi-discrete cells, as well as a couple tornadoes (primarily towards late afternoon and evening). This overall increasing threat will necessitate watch issuance within an hour or so.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for isolated damaging wind gusts and marginally severe hail continues for most of the areas covered by Severe Thunderstorm Watches #0312, 0313, and 0314 mainly over the southern and eastern portions of the area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms continue to cover an expansive area from southern VA to western ME with MLCAPE of 1000 (northeast) to 2500 (VA) J/kg and sufficient deep-layer shear continuing to support some organized bowing/supercellular characteristics, although most of the organized cells have been transient in nature. The tendency for outflows spreading quite rapidly from the storms despite the stronger deep-layer shear indicates the rather weak low-level winds and moderate evaporation occurring under cloud base is precluding any longer-lived organization. However, outside of the areas that have received expansive stabilization from the earlier storms (to be indicated in Watch Status updates shortly), the threat for isolated damaging winds and marginally severe hail will continue for the next few hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/severe storms will continue to build south into western Kansas, as well as east across Colorado, through this evening, with an attendant threat of severe winds, large hail, and a couple tornadoes. A new watch will eventually be needed south of ongoing Watch 315.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: In areas that have recovered following early-day outflow, two small bowing storms are progressing southeast around 40 kt over far northeast CO/southwest NE/northwest KS this afternoon. Further strengthening and upscale growth (with embedded supercells) is probable through late afternoon, given movement into a more buoyant low-level air mass. Multiple severe wind gusts and large hail would be the primary threats with these cells. To the west, further development may occur on both an outflow boundary over northeast Colorado and with convection building east from higher terrain into strengthening south/southeasterly low-level flow this evening. In addition to the wind and hail threat with these cells, elongating hodographs may support a couple tornadoes in any embedded supercells, primarily over western Kansas. The southeastward development of the entire severe threat will eventually require a new watch south of Watch 315. ..Picca.. 07/27/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms will continue to pose a risk for large hail and locally strong wind gusts through 02Z followed by a gradual diminishing trend. It appears coverage of storms/severe events will probably remain too sparse for a WW issuance, but trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Very isolated storms continue developing within a broad northwest flow regime from the northern Rockies through the central Plains of northern NE. A few subtle vorticity maxima, the higher terrain, and convective boundaries continue to serve as focusing mechanisms for initiation. Based on current surface observations with temperatures in the 70s and dewpoints in the 50s F, along with RAP forecast sounding, the storms are developing within a marginally unstable environment with 800-1200 J/kg MLCAPE along with modest (6.5-7.5 C/km) mid-level lapse rates. However, effective bulk shear from 45-50 kt and the discrete nature of the storms will continue to support a few supercell structures capable of large hail and locally strong downdrafts. Due to very sparse storm coverage and somewhat limited duration of the greater severe threat (next 3 hours or so), a WW will probably not be needed.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat persists across remaining portions of WWs 312, 313, and 314.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The severe threat continues along and ahead of a broken line of convection extending from southern New Hampshire southwestward to southeastern Pennsylvania and central Virginia. Occasional reports of wind/tree damage and 1-1.5 inch hailstones have been reported with the strongest convection over the past few hours with these storms. This threat should continue given the moderately unstable (2000-2500 J/kg) and moderately sheared (35-45 kt) pre-convective airmass. Over time (i.e., the next couple of hours) these storms may reach eastern portions of Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Long Island (New York) and pose a severe threat before the scheduled expiration times of each watch (02Z). If this scenario materializes, spatial extensions of the Watches (particularly WW 312) may be needed. Continued maturation of cold pools west of the ongoing storms will result in a decreased severe threat with time. Ongoing WWs in these areas may be cancelled early. ..Cook.. 07/27/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for a couple tornadoes, isolated large hail, and damaging wind will persist across WW 315 next couple hours. A more substantial severe/damaging wind threat may evolve over the southeastern portion of WW 315 and into severe thunderstorm watch 317 from east central Colorado through western KS into mid-evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early this evening, numerous storms are developing along a what appears to be a convectively reinforced boundary from north central KS into northeast CO. Mostly discrete supercell structures persist over KS. However, there has been a tendency for storms to congeal into a small cluster across northeast CO. The atmosphere across southeast CO into western KS remains moderately unstable with 1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE and is weakly capped. This along with a strengthening southerly nocturnal low-level jet will continue to support development along the consolidated outflows, and tendency should be for storms to grow upscale into a southward-advancing MCS. While large hail, and a couple tornadoes remain possible in the short term, greatest severe threat should transition to damaging wind. Farther north across the remainder of tornado watch 315 from southeast WY into western NE and far northeast CO, much of the boundary layer has been stabilized by convective outflow. However, latest objective analysis indicates the presence of moderate MUCAPE for parcels lifted from above the surface layer. Therefore storms over southeast WY will remain capable of producing mainly large hail as they move southeast and become elevated over top of the stable layer next couple hours. ..Dial.. 07/27/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for mainly damaging wind and some hail will continue to evolve across southwest KS next couple hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cluster of storms continues along the southeast CO to southwest KS border. An isolated supercell was located over southwest KS just northeast of dodge city along a southwest-surging outflow boundary. The 00Z RAOB from DDC indicated modest instability with around 1200 J/kg MLCAPE and an inversion near 650 mb. While this thermodynamic environment is not particularly impressive, especially given a stabilizing boundary layer, some increase in the low-level jet has occurred with latest DDC VWP data showing around 30 kt. Storms have been slow to evolve into an organized MCS, but numerous mergers are occurring, and consolidated cold pools along with the strengthening southerly low-level jet beneath northwest flow aloft will continue to support forward propagation into southwest KS next few hours. A swath of strong to damaging wind gusts remains possible, through overall threat does not appear as robust as earlier expected. ..Dial.. 07/28/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms will continue developing southeast next couple hours, eventually affecting parts of the OK and TX Panhandles into northwest OK. There is still some uncertainty regarding how much of a severe threat will exist south of ww 317, but current thinking is that storms will continue pose a risk for damaging wind. A WW will likely be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have consolidated into a small MCS over southwest KS along with a persistent supercell southeast of Dodge City. The storms are moving generally south at around 30-35 kt. Modest instability still persists in the downstream atmosphere with around 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE, but the boundary layer continues to stabilize. The somewhat marginal thermodynamic environment along with weaker winds aloft with southward extent into OK lower confidence to some degree in longevity of overall threat. However, storms remain severe with 66 kt recently reported at Syracuse KS and continue to organize along consolidated cold pool. This along with evidence of an MCV and rear inflow jet suggest storms may continue to pose a severe threat next few hours as they move south of WW 317.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for severe storms should continue to diminish over the next few hours. Additional watches are not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small MCS with an advancing cold pool continues to travel southeastward across northwest OK. Measured wind gusts have been in the 30-40 mph range with isolated gusts near 50 mph. The radar presentation has been diminishing gradually as these storms have only weak instability and storm relative inflow available. The air mass is a bit more moist to the southeast of the storm complex, but there is little large-scale support for re-organization. If trends continue, the watch may be canceled prior to scheduled 10Z expiration. ..Jewell.. 07/28/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
